standard_prerequisites.name: The recursion principle of truncation
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map from a type into an n-truncated type extends to the truncation of its source, and the extension sends a projection to the value of the original map.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies both the extension used in one direction and the equality checks in the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Function extensionality
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two maps are equal as soon as they agree on every argument.
standard_prerequisites.use: The two round-trip verifications are carried out pointwise on generators.

core_obligations: Given an n-truncated target B, extend any map f from A to B to a map from the truncation of A to B using the recursion principle (source line 549).
Show that the composite of the extension with the projection equals f, pointwise by the definition of the extension (source line 550).
Show that extending the composite of a map g with the projection returns g, by comparing both maps on a projection, which closes the equivalence (source line 551).

proof_roadmap.step: Extend a map along the projection by the recursion principle.
Verify the two round trips on generators.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 541-546: the universal property of truncation, that maps from the truncation of A into an n-truncated type are the maps from A. The proof (source lines 548-552) is short but it is a construction with both checks rather than a pointer: it extends a map by the recursion principle for truncations, then shows that the extension composed with the projection returns the original map on every point, and that extending a composite returns the same map by comparing the two on a generating projection. The construction and the two round-trip verifications are the substance, and the sequence of maps in the statement does not display them.
